key_insight: KaliBench shows that translating natural-language cybersecurity intent into exact Kali Linux commands is still hard, with minor CLI mistakes causing major execution failures.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark provides a practical way to train and evaluate agentic cybersecurity tools using deterministic, verifiable command outputs rather than vague end-task scores.
method: Built a fine-grained dataset of 8,504 query-command pairs covering 1,642 tools, 23 capability dimensions, and 5 security phases.
Used manuscript-grounded command generation with deterministic canonicalization and alias-aware evaluation to assess tool choice and argument construction.
Added multi-stage verification with LLM checks, sandboxed terminal execution, and human review, enabling runtime-free verifiable rewards.
evidence_signal: Across 24 model configurations, no open-weight model exceeded 42% exact-command accuracy in the unrestricted setting.
watch_item: Results may depend on command canonicalization and sandboxed verification rules, so deployment quality can vary if real tool environments differ from the benchmark.
paper_title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
